{{Nihongo|'''Masao Doi'''|土井正男|Doi Masao}} (born 29 March 1948) is a Professor Emeritus at [[Nagoya University]] and The [[University of Tokyo]]. He is a Fellow of the Toyota Physical and Chemical Research Institute.<ref name="home">{{citation|title=Home Page of Masao Doi|url=http://www11.ocn.ne.jp/~masaodoi/index_E.html|access-date=2013-03-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712150409/http://www11.ocn.ne.jp/~masaodoi/index_E.html|archive-date=2015-07-12|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1976, he introduced [[Second quantization|second quantized formalism]] for studying [[Reaction-diffusion system|reaction-diffusion]] systems, which is now known as the [[Doi–Peliti field theory]].<ref name="1976a">{{citation|title = Second quantization representation for classical many-body system|last1= Doi|first1= M.|journal=J. Phys. A: Math. Gen.|year=1976|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/9/9/008|volume=9|issue=9|page=1465}}</ref><ref name="1976b">{{citation |title = Stochastic theory of diffusion-controlled reaction|last1= Doi|first1= M.|journal=J. Phys. A: Math. Gen.|year=1976|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/9/9/009|volume=9|issue=9|page=1479|bibcode= 1976JPhA....9.1479D}}</ref> In 1978 and 1979 he wrote a series of papers with [[Sam Edwards (physicist)|Sir Sam Edwards]] expanding on the concept of [[reptation]] introduced by [[Pierre-Gilles de Gennes]] in 1971.<ref name="flow">{{Cite journal | last1 = Doi | first1 = M. | last2 = Edwards | first2 = S. F. | doi = 10.1039/f29787401789 | title = Dynamics of concentrated polymer systems. Part 1.?Brownian motion in the equilibrium state | journal = Journal of the Chemical Society, Faraday Transactions 2 | volume = 74 | pages = 1789–1801 | year = 1978 }}</ref><ref name="flow2"/><ref name="flow3"/><ref name="flow4"/>  In 1996 he authored the textbook ''Introduction to Polymer Physics''.<ref name="tbook">{{cite book | title=Introduction to Polymer Physics | author=Doi, M. | isbn=9780198517894 | lccn= <!-- 95014969 wrong number --> | series=Oxford Science Publications | year=1996 | publisher=Clarendon Press }}</ref>

== Recognition and awards ==
In 2001 the [[American Physical Society]] awarded Doi the Polymer Physics Prize for "pioneering contributions to the theory of dynamics and rheology of entangled polymers and complex
fluids."<ref name="aps">{{citation|title=2001 Polymer Physics Prize Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Masao&last_nm=Doi&year=2001|access-date=2013-03-01}}</ref>

He was also awarded the [[Bingham Medal]] in 2001 by the [[Society of Rheology]].<ref name= "BM"/>

In 2016, he was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions to the rheology of polymeric liquids, especially the entanglement effect in concentrated solutions and melts.
